rawFindings.title: Incorrect position of trailing comma error report in 'always-multiline' mode
rawFindings.explanation: In the checkForTrailingComma function, the code now uses lastTokenOnNewLine instead of nodeIsMultiLine to decide if the trailing comma position is valid. However, the error report for an unexpected trailing comma uses penultimateToken.loc.start, which may report the error at the comma token of the previous item instead of the actual trailing comma token when the comma is after the last property and on the same line.
rawFindings.suggestion: Change the error report location for unexpected trailing commas in 'always-multiline' mode from penultimateToken.loc.start to the actual token's location representing the trailing comma.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: For input code with a trailing comma in single-line object (e.g., var foo = {a:1, b:2,};), ESLint reports the error at the wrong column (the previous property's comma) instead of at the trailing comma token.
